plain_english_revision: **Core Change**: Transfers oversight of construction/renovation for most state colleges and universities from the state’s Division of Construction Management (DCM) to their governing boards. **Key Additions**
candidate_position_supported: **Policy Effect**: Expands institutional autonomy over campus infrastructure decisions for state colleges/universities, while mandating DCM’s electronic processes and tornado-safe space requirements for new dorm/classroom buildings.
evidence_quotes: ‘Any powers, authority, and jurisdiction granted to the Division of Construction Management within this section relating to an educational institution... is hereby transferred to the governing board of each institution’
‘The Division of Construction Management shall provide for the electronic submission and signing of documents. The bill would also require the division to make annual reports to the Legislature.’
‘any new contract awarded... shall include an Alabama Building Commission Division of Construction Management approved safe space or hallway rated for tornadoes’
review_reason: The amendment’s procedural scope (e.g., renumbering, line deletions) and reliance on cross-referenced sections make full intent ambiguous without the original bill text. The ‘nonideological’ valence assumes no partisan framing; context may reveal deeper policy implications.
